notes: Shared vocabulary for casualties, scenes and the illustration system. Content files may only use ids defined here.
Left/right always mean the casualty's own left/right, not the viewer's.
Every overlay is drawn exactly one way by the renderer, so casualties never carry art of their own.

adult.description: Adults and teenagers. Adult body proportions and adult sieve.

child.description: Roughly ages 1-10 (placeholder: confirm NZRT cut-off). Child body proportions and child sieve.

standing.description: Upright, facing the viewer. Walking wounded, bystanders.

sitting.description: On a low seat (kerb, block, crate or their wheelchair), back upright, knees bent, feet flat on the ground. Use for anyone sitting, including 'sitting on the ground' in approach text.

slumped.description: Seated like sitting, but the torso has slumped sideways or forward and the head has dropped. Usually a deterioration of sitting.

supine.description: Lying on the back, seen from above.

prone.description: Lying face down, seen from above. Face, chest, abdomen and groins are not visible.

recovery.description: Lying on the left side in the recovery position, top leg bent, head tilted. Only reached through the recovery_position action or a deterioration.

look.description: Base appearance so casualties are recognisable on a scene map. The renderer picks colours from a fixed muted palette that never uses the tag colours.

bleed.look: Dark maroon (#5e0b15) irregular stain with a fine diagonal hatch texture, so blood never reads as the red triage tag. minor: small patch. major: stain covering most of the region, slowly spreading. catastrophic: covers the region, pulses, and leaves a pool on the ground next to the region. Hidden bleeds appear inside a cut-away patch of clothing once revealed.

wound.look: laceration: short dark line with a thin pink margin. puncture: small dark circle. abrasion: rough-edged pink graze with speckles. No visible tissue.

deformity.look: The limb segment is drawn with a 25-degree kink at its midpoint. open=true adds a small puncture-style wound mark at the kink (no bone drawn).

amputation.look: The limb stops partway along the segment with a rounded, clothing-edged stump. Parts beyond it are not drawn. Pair it with a bleed finding on the same region unless already controlled.

swelling.look: Outward bulge of the region outline with a pale purple tint.

burn.look: superficial: pink tint. partial: pink-brown patch with small white blister circles. full: charcoal-grey leathery patch with cross-hatch. Never orange, to keep clear of the orange tag.

impaled_object.look: A grey (rebar, metal_sheet), pale blue (glass) or brown (wood) object protruding at an angle from the region centre, with a small dark ring where it enters.

soot.look: Grey-black smudges around the nose and mouth. Sign of smoke inhalation.

entrapment.look: Grey block shapes (rubble: broken chunks; beam: one long timber or steel bar; slab: one flat concrete block; vehicle: dark panel edge; furniture: a brown wooden shelf or cabinet outline) drawn over every covered region. Any overlay on a covered region is hidden underneath.

pallor.look: Skin desaturated and shifted toward grey; lips pale. Must still be noticeable on dark skin tones (grey lips and inner eyelids).

cyanosis.look: Blue-grey tint on lips and around the mouth.

sweating.look: Three or four small droplet shapes on the forehead and cheeks.

dust.look: Light grey speckle over skin and clothing.

wet.look: Darker clothing with a few drip shapes and flattened hair.

eyes.look: Eye shapes on the face. Default when not set: open if responsive is alert, otherwise closed.

expression.look: Mouth and brow shapes. Default when not set: calm if alert, blank otherwise.

motion.look: Short motion lines around the body; seizing adds a jagged outline. Purely visual cue, not animation-dependent.

speech.look: Speech bubble from the mouth, max about 40 characters. Something the casualty says without being asked.

mobility_aid.look: The person's own mobility aid on the ground beside the figure, in neutral grey and blue. A wheelchair is drawn side-on next to a sitting figure (or under them if the pose is sitting and the aid is intact). broken: wheelchair tipped with a buckled wheel; frame, crutches or stick bent with a snapped segment.

guarding.look: The casualty's opposite free hand is moved to hold or cradle this region.

breathing_animation.look: Chest outline (or the back, when the pose hides the chest) rises and falls at the revealed rate; flat with a 'no movement' mark when not breathing. Shallow or gasping depth changes the amplitude.

pulse_marker.look: Two-finger marker on the wrist with a small heart-beat glyph, or a crossed glyph when absent.

crt_marker.look: Fingertip marker with a small stopwatch glyph and the seconds.

response_bubble.look: Rounded response bubble (distinct from speech: dashed outline) showing the response to a check, e.g. 'Squeezes hand' or 'No response'.

callout.look: Small pinned label with a leader line to the region. Every revealed finding gets one; tapping it jumps to its triage card field.

tourniquet.look: Black band with a windlass bar, placed toward the body end of the segment, plus a small time label.

wound_packing.look: White gauze pushed into the wound site with a hand pressing on it.

hand_pressure.look: Gloved hand (rescuer: purple glove), bare hand (bystander) or the casualty's own free hand (self, same as guarding plus a white pad) pressing on the region.

airway_open.look: Head tilted back with a small chin-lift arrow.

triage_tag.look: Tag on the wrist in the category colour with the category's text label printed on it, never colour alone.

splint.look: Two straight boards along the segment held with white ties.

cervical_collar.look: Rigid collar band around the neck.

cracking_wall.description: Wall or ceiling visibly cracking, dust falling.

gas_smell.description: Strong smell of gas; may hiss.

aftershock.description: Ground shaking; loose material may fall.

downed_power_line.description: Fallen line on the ground, possibly live.

rising_water.description: Flood water or tsunami surge rising.

chemical_spill.description: Unknown liquid or vapour, odd smell, people coughing. Withdraw upwind and uphill.

machinery.description: Machinery still running or able to move.

rockfall.description: Rocks or mud still coming down the slope.

bystanderBehaviours.pulls_to_friend: Keeps grabbing the rescuer and insisting they treat a specific casualty first.
bystanderBehaviours.panicking: Uninjured or minor injury, distressed, loud, may block access.
bystanderBehaviours.helper: Calm, willing to hold pressure or keep an airway open if instructed.
bystanderBehaviours.parent: Parent or carer of a child casualty; can give identity and history.
bystanderBehaviours.filming: Filming on a phone, ignores instructions.
bystanderBehaviours.obstructive: Tries to move or pull a casualty out, or gets in the way.
bystanderBehaviours.walking_wounded_helper: Has a minor injury, already tagged green, can be given a simple task.

sceneEvents.hazard_appears: A hazard from the hazards list appears or gets worse.
sceneEvents.aftershock: Shaking. Usually paired with a hazard and a correct response.
sceneEvents.new_casualty: A casualty arrives or is discovered.
sceneEvents.radio_message: Instruction or information over the radio.
sceneEvents.casualty_calls_out: A casualty out of view calls or stops calling out.
sceneEvents.signal: A whistle or horn signal from vocab.signals. Usually a quick-time event.

notes: Flat, friendly, schematic figures with consistent 2px outlines. No photos and no gore.
Tag colours (red, orange, green, black) are reserved for tags and UI. Clothing, blood, burns and props never use them.
Blood is dark maroon with a hatch texture so it never reads as a red tag.
Child figures use child proportions (larger head, shorter limbs) on the same skeleton so every overlay anchors the same way.

signals.notes: Whistle or horn signals used at the scene. Defaults follow the international USAR (INSARAG) signals; confirm NZRT's before relying on them. blasts are lengths in seconds, played as audio cues.

cease.meaning: Stop all work and be quiet so the team can listen for survivors

resume.pattern: One long and one short blast

localHazards.notes: Dangers right next to one casualty, found by check_danger at that casualty. Skipping the check means the rescuer meets the hazard.
localHazards.sharp_metal: Torn sheet metal or exposed rebar
localHazards.fuel_spill: Fuel or oil leaking onto the ground

event.cue: The ground lurches and everything around you starts to shake.
event.followUpCue: The shaking stops. Dust is drifting down from the damaged structure beside you.
event.description: An aftershock while you were working.

event.cue: You notice a smell of gas, and it is getting stronger.
event.description: A gas leak near where you were working.

event.cue: You smell petrol and see a pool spreading under the wreck towards you.
The water around your boots is suddenly rising fast.

qtePoolNotes: Random quick-time events added when the player turns them on: matched to a scene by its tags and the words in its briefing type and hazards. cue is what the player senses; it must never name the answer.
